title: Scorecard + causal rollback recommender for SLO-driven rollouts
creator: Alyssa Kim
description:
Summary: We need an automated rollback recommender that scores rollout candidates using a calibrated set of SLO signals (latency p95, error rate, per-request token cost, throughput). The recommender will run a lightweight causal decomposition (difference-in-differences + regression residuals) to attribute degradations to model changes versus traffic or routing shifts, and emit an explainable score and remediation suggestion (reduce traffic, revert model variant, or pause rollout). This ticket covers design, experiment harness, and MVP integration.

Goals and acceptance criteria: Produce a 0-100 risk score per evaluation window with an explanation bundle (top 3 signals and causal attribution). Support weighted multi-signal policies and composite thresholds. Integrate with rollout controller to surface soft recommendations and optional auto-rollback. Validate on shadow and 1% canary traffic with historical and synthetic regressions. Provide Console dashboards: score timeseries, cohort breakdown, and contribution heatmap.

Design notes and trade-offs: Use pragmatic causal methods for speed and explainability; normalize signals by cohort and time-of-day; emit natural-language rationale. Keep CPU/memory bounded to run inside rollout worker; no heavy offline training for MVP. Require conservative safety hysteresis for auto-rollback.

MVP implementation plan: 1) data plumbing: add cohort-tagged timeseries (route, region, client-type, model-variant) to short-term evaluation store; 2) scoring engine: Scorecard Rust worker computing normalized deltas, small regression, and diff-in-diff test; 3) policy layer: extend rollout controller to accept composite SLO policies (weights, threshold, hysteresis); 4) Console: UI card with latest score, contributors, and one-click rollback; 5) safety net: auto-rollback behind org-level enable flag (default off).

Progress: 2026-03-10 kickoff and PRD draft. 2026-03-11 instrumentation spike: cohort keys added to metrics exporter (internal PR). 2026-03-12 prototype Scorecard worker: normalized delta and weighted aggregation implemented and run against past incident. 2026-03-13 design review with Console team: show recommendation state machine rather than raw scores.

Open questions/risks: calibration data scarcity; false positives leading to availability loss (mitigate with consecutive-window requirement and cohort consensus); cohort sparsity (fallback to aggregate with low confidence).

Experiment plan: Phase A shadow 2 weeks (no UI exposure); Phase B canary 0.5-1% show recommendations to SRE; Phase C opt-in auto-rollback for internal teams behind feature flag with FP rate <2% for 30 days before wider rollout.

Acceptance metrics: precision >=85% on canary, recall >=80% on held-out incidents, MTTR improvement vs baseline.

Artifacts: PRD in Confluence (internal), metrics PR, prototype branch, Grafana dashboard mock.

Next steps: finish Scorecard unit tests (2d), wire policy into rollout controller and add org-level API for enabling auto-rollback (3d), prepare shadow-phase runbook and oncall playbook.

Reviewer asks: engineering leads review causal approach and computational profile; PM/Console review UI copy and filters for 'auto-rollback-enabled' rollouts.

Comments: Marco Hernández (2026-03-12): "Prototype looks good; add CPU/memory limits and confidence bands for noisy cohorts." Priya Anand (PM, 2026-03-13): "Add Console label and filter for auto-rollback-enabled rollouts."

Longer-term: add richer causal discovery with model logits and input-length instrumentation, targeted rollback recommendations between model variants, and programmatic scoring plugin API for trusted customers.
